title: Extended community pharmacy opening hours: budget impact and how the service works in practice
subtitle: Systematic review in two strands for a commissioning decision
statement: A regional health authority must decide by March 2027 whether to pay about 2.1 million a year for 40 community pharmacies to open late on weekdays and on Sundays. The claimed savings from avoided out-of-hours GP contacts and emergency department visits are uncertain and mostly estimated by pharmacy bodies, and the practicalities of late-night staffing are contested. A systematic review is needed that keeps the budget impact evidence and the evidence on how the service works in practice separate, then brings them together for the board.
whoAffected: Residents who need medicines or advice out of hours, especially shift workers and people without a registered GP; community pharmacists and owners; out-of-hours GP and emergency department services; the commissioning board and its budget.
whatHurts: Paying for a service that does not reduce demand elsewhere would divert money from other care; refusing a service that reaches people with nowhere else to go could push them to emergency departments; unsafe lone working could harm pharmacy staff.
currentPractice: A few pharmacies open late on their own account; out-of-hours minor ailments and emergency supply go to the out-of-hours GP service or emergency departments; previous commissioning papers relied on advocacy estimates.
whyNow: A board decision in March 2027 and one funded analyst from October 2026 to March 2027.
constraints: One analyst for six months; no primary data collection; local re-pricing needs the data governance lead's approval, not yet requested; the two strands must not be merged into one number.
patientCenteredGoal: People who need medicines or advice in the evening or on Sunday can get them safely and close to home, and the authority spends its budget where it reduces unmet need.
summary: Problem framed as a systematic review with a budget impact strand and a practice-and-views strand for a funding decision.
